# SetCameraProjectionMatrix

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Cameras](Blitz3D-Cameras)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetCameraProjectionMatrix:Void camera:Int32, matrix:FloatMatrix4x4
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | In | Int32 | required | Camera handle. |
| `matrix` | In | FloatMatrix4x4 | required | The projection matrix. |

## Description

Gives a camera a projection matrix of its own. It replaces [CameraZoom](CameraZoom), [CameraRange](CameraRange) and [CameraProjMode](CameraProjMode) until [ResetCameraProjectionMatrix](ResetCameraProjectionMatrix) is called; they can still be changed meanwhile and are used again after the reset. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

The matrix uses the usual convention: the camera looks down +Z, X is to the right and Y up, and the depth goes from 0 at the near plane to 1 at the far plane. `m[column][row]` is one number. For a perspective matrix the fourth row is `0, 0, 1, 0`, for an orthographic one `0, 0, 0, 1`. BlitzLLVM turns it into what the GPU needs itself, so the same matrix works on every renderer.

What it is good for:

* A near and far plane that [CameraRange](CameraRange) can't give, or a view that is not the same on both sides.
* Pictures bigger than the screen: render the view in tiles, each with a matrix that shows one part of it, into a texture ([SetCameraBuffer](SetCameraBuffer)), and put the tiles together.
* Mirrors and portals, with a matrix whose near plane is the mirror.

The engine still needs a near and a far plane for fog, soft sprite edges and culling, and reads them out of the matrix: they are exact for a usual perspective or orthographic matrix and close for others. A camera with a matrix of its own draws even with `CameraProjMode camera, 0`. [CameraPick](CameraPick) and [CameraProject](CameraProject) use the matrix too.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5
; The same picture as CameraZoom 1 and CameraRange 1, 1000, written out.
Local near# = 1, far# = 1000
Local m:FloatMatrix4x4
m[0][0] = 1
m[1][1] = 320.0 / 240.0
m[2][2] = far / (far - near)
m[2][3] = 1
m[3][2] = -far * near / (far - near)
SetCameraProjectionMatrix camera, m
RenderWorld
Flip
```
